text: Nearly a thousand PhDs got this puzzle wrong. Your turn.
Picture three briefcases. One holds a million dollars, and two are empty.
That's a hundred bucks a day. For twenty-seven years.
You pick a case. But the host knows where the money is.
And he always opens an empty case you didn't pick.
Then he asks: stay with yours, or switch? Hit like if it feels fifty-fifty.
A columnist printed the answer in nineteen ninety: switch.
By her count, nearly a thousand PhDs wrote in to say she was wrong.
Let's check every— every possible start.
One: you picked the money. The other case is empty, so switching loses.
Send this to the friend who'd stop listening now.
Two: you picked an empty case. So he has to open the other empty one, and switching wins.
Three: you picked the other empty case, so switching wins again.
That's two wins out of three.
Make it a hundred cases. You pick one, and he opens ninety-eight empties.
Now switching wins ninety-nine percent of the time.
So… stay or switch? Your turn.
